study_type_evidence.quote: mice (n = 6) received a single s.c. administration of 300‐nmol·kg−1 mGIPAnt‐1
Animals received a daily s.c. injection at 4:30 PM with mGIPAnt‐1 (300‐nmol·kg−1) or vehicle.
COS‐7 cells were cultured at 10% CO2 and 37°C in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium 1885

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female C57Bl/6Jrj, 8 weeks old at arrival; PK cohort n = 6; ovariectomised at 9 weeks and placed on HFD or control diet at 10 weeks for the chronic arm
in_vivo_species.quote: Female C57Bl/6Jrj mice (8 weeks old) were obtained from Janvier Labs (Saint Berthevin Cedex, France)

in_vitro_detail: COS-7 cells transiently transfected with human or mouse GIP receptor, or with mouse GLP-1 or GLP-2 receptor, assayed for cAMP accumulation (HitHunter cAMP assay) to establish antagonist potency and absence of intrinsic activity; n = 5 independent experiments.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: mGIPAnt‐1 pharmacokinetics following subcutaneous (s.c.) administration of 6‐nmol mGIPAnt‐1
concentration_time_figure.note: Plasma mGIPAnt-1 concentration versus time after a single s.c. dose. Because each mouse could only be bled a limited number of times, the full 0-32 h elimination curve was assembled from three staggered sampling windows (0-2.5, 2.5-22 and 22-32 h).

bioanalytical_method: In-house radioimmunoassay (RIA) with a polyclonal mid-regional anti-GIP antibody (code no. 95234) and 125I-monolabelled human GIP(1-42) tracer, using mGIPAnt-1 as the standard
bioanalytical_quote: mGIPAnt‐1 levels were measured by an in‐house radioimmunoassay using a polyclonal antibody recognizing a mid‐regional part of GIP (code no. 95234)
notes: The half-life is a genuine half-life in time units reported by the authors, not a rate constant: the Methods state 'Half‐life (t½) of mGIPAnt‐1 administered s.c. was, determined from the concentration versus time curves after semi‐logarithmical transformation and calculated with the following formulas: k = (ln (Ct1) − ln (Ct2))/𝛥t and t½ = ln(2)/k with Ct1 at t = 1.5 h and Ct2 at t = 32 h'. The conversion was done by the authors, not by the curator. half_life_phase is recorded as 'elimination' because the fit spans 1.5-32 h and the Results state the sampling design was used 'To obtain the full elimination curve'; the 1.5 h peak marks the end of absorption, so no absorption half-life exists and half_life_absorption is 'not reported'. tmax = 1.5 h is a genuine body-reported time to peak; no Cmax concentration value is printed anywhere in the body (the y-axis values are only in Figure 3a). Dose bookkeeping: the PK Methods say 300 nmol/kg while the Results and Figure 3a caption say 6 nmol per mouse - both are recorded verbatim in the dose field without reconciling them. Procedural agents not given agent objects: carprofen (5 mg/kg s.c. analgesia), isoflurane anaesthesia, and terminal ketamine/xylazine (90/10 mg/kg i.p.). No ex vivo assay (no serum or plasma stability experiment) is described in the body.
